title: bug: a deployed candidate container receives no environment variables at all
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 at HEAD 7622a2e8 by worker-bcaa6d5e from the epic-final row task-99f364e3, driving the real pipeline against real docker 29.6.2.

THE SYMBOL: `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-service.ts`
  export const runCandidateArgv = (name, network, tag) => ["run", "--detach", "--name", name, "--network", network, tag];
No `--env`, no `--env-file`, no `--env` derived from the environment store. `startCandidate` calls exactly this argv and nothing else on the deploy path delivers variables to the container it starts.

WHY THAT IS A CROSS-BAND DEFECT AND NOT A DESIGN CHOICE. Three consumers spell the same variable identically and two of them get it:
- the scaffold's app reads `process.env.DATABASE_URL` (controlled-profile-package-templates.ts:179);
- `docker-compose.override.yml` delivers `DATABASE_URL: ${DATABASE_URL:?set DATABASE_URL in .env}` to the COMPOSE-managed `app` service, so the INCUMBENT has it;
- `deploy-migration-context.ts:39` reads `DATABASE_URL` back out of the encrypted store, so the MIGRATION has it.
The one process that does NOT have it is the container `deployment.deploy` promotes to serve production traffic. The secrets band stores the variables, the migration band consumes them, and the deploy band never hands them to the app it starts.

CORROBORATED FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION: the canary sweep in `tests/e2e/foundation/platform-secret-canary.e2e.test.ts` inspects the candidate container's `docker inspect` configuration and finds no planted value — a clean DoD-5 result that is simultaneously the evidence for this defect.

WHY IT HAS NOT REDDED ANYTHING YET: the generated `/health` route is a pure function that touches no database, so a candidate with no DATABASE_URL still reports healthy and still passes the deploy's own gate. Any route that reads the database would fail in production after a deploy that reported DEPLOYED.

DEFINITION OF DONE
1. The candidate container receives the environment the store holds for its environment, through the same `readEnvironmentDelivery` seam the migration already uses — not a second reading of the variables and not a file written next to the build context.
2. No variable value reaches a log line, a receipt, an error path or a `docker inspect` output as a result. The existing canary sweep must still find zero hits.
3. An arm proves DELIVERY TO THE CANDIDATE by response, not by argv inspection: a route on the deployed build that echoes a non-secret marker taken from the environment.
4. Existing deploy arms stay green: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, and `MOE_PLATFORM_PIPELINE=1 npx vitest run tests/e2e/foundation/platform-pipeline.e2e.test.ts --no-file-parallelism`.
definitionOfDone: The candidate container started by deployment.deploy receives the environment variables the encrypted store holds for that environment, resolved through the same readEnvironmentDelivery seam the migration path already uses.

No variable value reaches a log line, a deploy receipt, an error path or docker inspect output: tests/e2e/foundation/platform-secret-canary.e2e.test.ts still reports hits=0 with its candidate-inspect sweep intact.
Delivery to the candidate is proven BY RESPONSE from the running deployed build, not by inspecting the argv the engine assembled.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with its count line quoted, and MOE_PLATFORM_PIPELINE=1 vitest run tests/e2e/foundation/platform-pipeline.e2e.test.ts --no-file-parallelism stays green.

implementationPlan.description:
CONFIRM THE DEFECT AND THE CONSTRAINT THAT DECIDES THE DESIGN. NO EDITS.

(a) THE DEFECT. Read apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-service.ts:69-71. `runCandidateArgv` is `["run", "--detach", "--name", name, "--network", network, tag]` — no `--env`, no `--env-file`, no mount. `startCandidate` (:228-233) calls exactly that and nothing else on the deploy path hands variables to the container. Confirm by reading, and confirm the migration DOES get them through `readEnvironmentDelivery` (deploy-migration-context.ts:3, :137) so the asymmetry the filing describes is real.

(b) THE CONSTRAINT, AND IT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. RE-RUN THIS — it takes ten seconds and it is the fact every later step rests on. `docker create --env CANARY=<a value> <any local image>` then `docker inspect <name> | grep -c <value>`. Measured at plan time on this host, docker 29.6.2: **1 hit**, the value printed inside `.Config.Env`. Now repeat with the value in a bind-mounted file instead (`--mount type=bind,source=<a path OUTSIDE the workspace>,target=/run/moe/env,readonly`): **0 hits** — `.Mounts` shows only the source PATH.

WHAT THAT MEANS, and why it is not optional: platform-secret-canary.e2e.test.ts:218 sweeps `docker inspect <candidate>` stdout for the planted value and :232 asserts ZERO hits. So DoD 1 and DoD 2 are jointly satisfiable by EXACTLY ONE family of designs — the values reach the container through a MOUNTED FILE, never through `--env` or `--env-file`. Any argv-based delivery turns this row's own DoD 2 red. The description's "not a file written next to the build context" is the same instruction from the other side: a file, yes, but outside the build context so it can never be committed or swept as a fixture.

(c) NAME EVERY ASSERTING CONSUMER OF THE ARGV BEFORE YOU CHANGE IT (project rail 20 — grep the SHAPE, not just the symbol). `runCandidateArgv` is pinned by deploy-service.test.ts:160 and by deploy-rollback.test.ts:111, :125 and :142, the last of which indexes into the argv positionally. All four are in this plan's files. If you find a fifth, stop and report rather than taking the extra path.

Record (a), the two grep counts from (b), and the consumer list in the step note.
implementationPlan.note: STEP 1 — DEFECT CONFIRMED, CONSTRAINT RE-MEASURED, AND TWO NEW FACTS THAT CHANGE THE SHAPE. No edits. (b) THE CONSTRAINT, re-run on this host, docker 29.6.2, image moe-deploy-preview:6cccf26a…: `docker create --name N --env CANARY_PROBE= ` then `docker inspect N | grep -c ` => **1** same value via `--mount type=bind,source=,target=/run/moe/env,readonly` => **0** Reproduces the plan's measurement exactly. platform-secret-canary.e2e.test.ts:218 sweeps candidate `docker inspect` stdout and :232 asserts zero hits, so argv-based delivery is excluded. Mounted file it is. (b2) TWO FACTS THE PLAN DID NOT HAVE, both measured, both change step 2's shape: 1. THE IMAGE ALREADY HAS AN ENTRYPOINT. `docker inspect --format '{{json .Config.Entrypoint}}|{{json .Config.Cmd}}'` on a real deployed image => `["docker-entrypoint.sh"]|["node","/app/dist/server.js"]`. The generated Dockerfile sets no ENTRYPOINT, but the node base image does. The plan's "exec form with NO entrypoint script" is true of the Dockerfile, not of the image. 2. `--entrypoint` CLEARS THE IMAGE CMD. Measured: `docker create --entrypoint X ` reports `.Config.Cmd = null`. So a command override CANNOT just `exec "$@"` — there are no args left. The original argv must be read back off the image (`docker image inspect --format '{{json .Config.Entrypoint}}\n{{json .Config.Cmd}}'`) and passed explicitly. (b3) THE SHAPE, PROVEN END TO END BEFORE WRITING ANY CODE. Real image, real container: `docker run --detach --name N --mount type=bind,source=,target=/run/moe/env,readonly --entrypoint /bin/sh -c 'set -a; . /run/moe/env; set +a; exec "$0" "$@"' docker-entrypoint.sh node /app/dist/server.js` => run ok; `health=healthy` (the image HEALTHCHECK survives the override, as predicted — it comes from the image, not CMD); `/proc/1/environ` contains `CANARY_PROBE=`; `docker inspect N | grep -c ` => **0**; `docker logs` empty. NOTE FOR LATER STEPS: `docker exec N printenv CANARY_PROBE` prints EMPTY even on success — exec builds its environment from the image Config.Env, not from PID 1's. So an exec-based probe would have read as a FALSE NEGATIVE here. /proc/1/environ is the correct in-container check, and DoD 3's response-based proof is the correct external one. Also confirmed /bin/sh exists in the image. Probe containers and temp files removed; `docker ps -a | grep -c moeprobe` => 0. (b4) REJECTED ON MEASUREMENT, recorded so it is not re-litigated: `docker create` + `docker cp -` (tar over stdin) + `docker start`. It is strictly better on secrecy (no host plaintext at all) and is the only shape that also works for a REMOTE (sshTarget) target, since a host bind-mount source does not exist on the remote docker host. I built and ran the tar writer. REJECTED because it changes the candidate's docker VERB from `run` to `create`/`start`, and the verb is pinned far beyond the four consumers the plan named — deploy-journey.test.ts:660 (`some(call[0]==="run")` toBe(true)), deploy-refusal-redaction.test.ts:325 (`failVerb("run")`), deploy-build-authority.test.ts:31, deploy-rollback.test.ts:183, deploy-service.test.ts:552/779/812/850, plus the double's dispatch at deploy-ports.ts:341. That is a rail-20 stop-and-report situation; the bind-mount shape keeps the census at exactly the four the architect named, which is why it wins. CONSEQUENCE TO BE HANDLED IN STEP 2: a REMOTE target cannot bind-mount a daemon-host path. Step 2 refuses explicitly and fail-closed in that case rather than mounting a path docker would silently auto-create as an empty DIRECTORY (which would fail as a 150s health timeout); a follow-up row will be filed for remote delivery. implementationPlan.description:
DELIVER THE ENVIRONMENT TO THE CANDIDATE THROUGH A MOUNTED FILE (DoD 1 + DoD 2 together — they are one design, not two).

In apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-service.ts, `startCandidate` resolves the environment through `readEnvironmentDelivery` — the SAME seam the migration uses (deploy-migration-context.ts:137), not a second reading of the store — writes it to a file OUTSIDE the build context, and mounts that file read-only into the candidate.

FORWARD EVERY REFUSAL UNCHANGED. `readEnvironmentDelivery` refuses with `ENV_NAME_INVALID` or `ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE` and its own layer; deploy-migration-context.ts:119 already establishes that these are forwarded verbatim rather than restated. A candidate that starts with a PARTIAL environment is worse than one that refuses — the delivery seam says so in its own comment at :124-126, and the deploy must inherit that: no partial delivery, no silent empty map.

THE RECOMMENDED SHAPE, because it needs no change to the generated image at all: keep the values out of `Config.Env` by having the container's own command load the file. The generated Dockerfile ends `CMD ["node", "${DEPLOYMENT_ENTRY_PATH}"]` (deployment-infrastructure-templates.ts:92) in exec form with no entrypoint script, so overriding the command to a shell that sources the mounted file and then `exec`s the same entry keeps `process.env` semantics IDENTICAL between candidate and incumbent — which is the property that matters, since the same app code has to work under both. `docker inspect` will then show the COMMAND (a path) and the MOUNT (a path), never a value. VERIFY, do not assume: that the image has a shell, that the override does not disturb the image's HEALTHCHECK (`healthArgv` reads `.State.Health.Status`, which comes from the image, not from CMD), and that the container still reaches healthy.

IF THAT SHAPE FAILS ON MEASUREMENT, the fallback is an entrypoint script baked into the generated image; say what failed and why before taking it, because it widens the row into the scaffold generator and its assertions.

THE FILE IS PLAINTEXT ON DISK FOR THE CONTAINER'S LIFETIME. Create it with an owner-only mode, outside the workspace, named so two concurrent deploys cannot collide, and remove it when the candidate is gone. Say in a comment what removes it. The canary already sanctions exactly one plaintext location — the workspace `.env`, gitignored (its assertion at :247) — so a second one has to justify itself in the code.

DO NOT USE `--env` OR `--env-file`. Step 1(b) measured that both put the value in `docker inspect`.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 2 — DELIVERY LANDED AS A MOUNTED FILE PLUS A COMMAND OVERRIDE. `pnpm typecheck` leg for the daemon (`npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/daemon/tsconfig.json`) EXIT 0.

THE SHAPE, exactly as measured in step 1(b3):
  run --detach --name N --network X
      --mount type=bind,source=<host file>,target=/run/moe/env,readonly
      --entrypoint /bin/sh <tag> -c "set -a; . /run/moe/env; set +a; exec \"$0\" \"$@\"" <image Entrypoint ++ Cmd>
`docker inspect` then shows a shell path, a loader string that contains no name and no value, and a mount SOURCE path. Nothing else changes: the incumbent and the candidate end up with the same `process.env` semantics because the image's own argv is what gets exec'd.

NEW FILE `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-environment.ts` (204 lines) holds the whole design and its header carries the measurement, so the next reader does not have to rediscover why `--env` is unusable:
  - `encodeCandidateEnvironment` — POSIX single-quoting (`'` closed/escaped/reopened). This is the ONE place an operator value becomes shell text; `$(whoami)`, backticks, `;`, newlines are all inert inside single quotes. Names are NOT re-checked: `readEnvironmentDelivery` already refuses ENV_NAME_INVALID for anything outside /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$/, and a second grammar is a second place to drift.
  - `runCandidateArgv(name, network, tag, mount = null)` — moved here, RE-EXPORTED from deploy-service.ts so every existing import path still works.
  - `imageCommandArgv` / `parseImageCommand` — because step 1 measured that `--entrypoint` CLEARS `.Config.Cmd`. Format is two JSON lines (`{{json .Config.Entrypoint}}\n{{json .Config.Cmd}}`) rather than `{{json .Config}}`, which would also hand us the image's Env.
  - `resolveCandidateMount(run, sshTarget, tag, source)` — takes the engine's own runner rather than importing one, so this module performs no effect it was not handed.
  - `candidateEnvironmentPort(config)` — reads through `readEnvironmentDelivery`, the SAME seam deploy-migration-context.ts:137 uses, and writes the file.

FORWARDING AND FAIL-CLOSED, per the step:
  - An environment refusal is forwarded as `${code}@${layer}` verbatim (`ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE@KEY`, `ENV_NAME_INVALID@NAME`), never restamped — the same convention deploy-migration-context.ts:119 set.
  - NO PARTIAL DELIVERY IS POSSIBLE: `readEnvironmentDelivery` refuses the WHOLE read on one unopenable seal, and the refusal is returned rather than degraded to an empty map. There is no `?? {}` and no catch-to-undefined anywhere on this path (that is exactly the `launchDelivery` mistake deploy-migration-context.ts's header warns about).
  - THE RESOLUTION HAPPENS BEFORE THE MIGRATION, not after: it reads the same store the migration is about to read, so an unopenable store refuses while the schema is still where the code expects it.

THE PLAINTEXT FILE: `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "moe-deploy-env-"))` — outside the workspace and outside every build context, so it can never be committed or swept as a fixture; the random directory makes two concurrent deploys collision-free; the file is written with `mode: 0o600`. WHAT REMOVES IT is stated in a comment at both ends: the `finally` of `execute()`, on EVERY exit path (success, refusal, throw), because the loader reads the mount once at startup and the candidate carries no restart policy. The daemon dying mid-deploy leaves one file in the OS temp directory — the same exposure class as any interrupted process, and bounded by the deploy window rather than the container's lifetime.

ZERO VARIABLES IS NOT A MOUNT. `source === null` when the environment holds nothing, and the argv is then BYTE-IDENTICAL to what it always was. That preserves environment-delivery.ts's own "delivery must not become a dependency" property at this seam too, and it is why the four rail-20 consumers stay green (verified: `npx vitest run --root apps/daemon --config package.json src/deployment/deploy-service.test.ts src/deployment/deploy-rollback.test.ts` => `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 56 passed (56)`).

REMOTE TARGETS REFUSE, EXPLICITLY. A bind mount names a path on the DOCKER host, and a remote target's docker host is not the daemon's. `resolveCandidateMount` returns DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_REMOTE_UNSUPPORTED when `sshTarget !== null` and there is something to deliver. Mounting anyway would be WORSE than refusing: docker AUTO-CREATES a missing bind source as an empty DIRECTORY, so the candidate would start, fail to read its delivery, and present as a 150s health timeout with no hint of the cause. A remote target with no variables still deploys exactly as before. A follow-up row for remote delivery is filed in step 6.

ROLLBACK GETS THE SAME TREATMENT (architect risk #5). `deploy-service.rollback()` re-enters `execute()`, so it already inherits `startCandidate`; the gap was that `rollback-command.ts:183` composed only `productionDeployPorts(...)`. implementationPlan.description:
PROVE DELIVERY BY RESPONSE FROM THE RUNNING DEPLOYED BUILD (DoD 3). This is the clause that separates a real fix from an argv that merely looks right.

DoD 3 is deliberate: "proven BY RESPONSE from the running deployed build, not by inspecting the argv the engine assembled." The generated `/health` route is a pure function that touches nothing (which is exactly why this defect never redded anything), so it cannot carry the proof. Add a route to the generated app that echoes a NON-SECRET marker read from its own environment — the scaffold templates are where the app's routes are declared — and have the pipeline arm set that marker in the store, deploy, and read it back over HTTP from the candidate.

THE MARKER IS NOT A SECRET AND MUST NOT LOOK LIKE ONE. Follow the canary file's own reasoning (:33-35): a plausible credential committed to a test tree trips real scanners and becomes its own incident. Use an obviously-inert name and value, and keep it distinct from the canary's `canary-not-a-secret-<12 hex>` shape so the two proofs cannot be confused for each other.

WHY A ROUTE AND NOT `docker exec ... printenv`: an exec proves the container's environment, which is close, but DoD 3 asks for the DEPLOYED BUILD's response — the app process actually reading its own `process.env` and answering on the port the proxy will flip to. That is the thing production depends on, and an exec would pass even if the app were started in a way that never inherited the values.

Keep this arm behind the same `MOE_PLATFORM_PIPELINE=1` gate as its neighbours, and heed the header at :42-47: these live files bind real host ports and cannot run in parallel with each other.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 4 — DoD 3 PROVEN BY RESPONSE FROM THE RUNNING DEPLOYED BUILD. GREEN.

`MOE_PLATFORM_PIPELINE=1 npx vitest run tests/e2e/foundation/platform-pipeline.e2e.test.ts --no-file-parallelism` => EXIT 0, `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 6 passed (6)`, 132.97s. Its own stdout: `PLATFORM PIPELINE server=29.6.2 shaA=00694bb9012d… shaB=52a51d5b268c…` / `PLATFORM PIPELINE deployed=build-b-b1206092 rolledBackTo=build-a-b1173f2f`. Real docker, real compose, real build, real encrypted store, real migration, real deploy AND real rollback.

THE ROUTE. `withDeliveryRoute` in platform-pipeline-harness.ts, added beside the existing `withBuildRoute` and applied by `materialize`, injects into the generated server:
    if (url === "/delivered") { return { status: 200, body: JSON.stringify({ marker: process.env.MOE_DELIVERY_MARKER ?? null }) }; }
`process.env` is read INSIDE the handler, at request time — a build-time literal would answer identically for a container that never received anything, which is the whole defect. The route names ONE non-secret variable and echoes nothing else; an always-on (flagless) arm asserts both properties, including `not.toContain("DATABASE_URL")`.
I did NOT widen into the scaffold generator, and the step's "the scaffold templates are where the app's routes are declared" is the one place I departed from it. `withBuildRoute` is the file's own precedent for a marker route added to the tree at materialize time, the injected route IS compiled into the deployed image (so DoD 3's "a route on the deployed build" is satisfied literally), and going through the generator would have widened this row into deployment/controlled-profile generator assertions for no gain in proof.

THE MARKER. `delivered-not-a-secret-<12 hex>`, minted per run, deliberately a DIFFERENT shape from the canary's `canary-not-a-secret-<12 hex>` so a hit can never be mistaken for the other proof. No scheme, no `@`, no `password=` — nothing a credential scanner would classify.

THE PROOF, and why it cannot pass vacuously:
  1. NEGATIVE CONTROL FIRST, before anything is delivered: the compose-managed INCUMBENT serves the same build and answers `/delivered` with `{"marker": null}`. So the later assertion cannot be satisfied by the image, by a hard-coded route, or by the incumbent still holding the port.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
THE DEFECT REPRODUCES BY READING, AND THE DESIGN IS DECIDED BY A MEASUREMENT I RAN.

THE DEFECT (confirmed at HEAD): apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-service.ts:69-71 is `runCandidateArgv = (name, network, tag) => ["run", "--detach", "--name", name, "--network", network, tag]`. No `--env`, no `--env-file`, no mount. `startCandidate` at :228-233 calls exactly that. The filing's asymmetry is real: deploy-migration-context.ts:3 and :137 resolve the environment through `readEnvironmentDelivery`, so the MIGRATION gets the variables and the container promoted to serve traffic does not.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDES EVERYTHING, run on this host against docker 29.6.2 (the same runtime the canary uses):
  `docker create --name <n> --env CANARY_PROBE=canary-not-a-secret-deadbeef1234 <local image>` then `docker inspect <n> | grep -c canary-not-a-secret-deadbeef1234` => **1**. `.Config.Env` printed `["CANARY_PROBE=canary-not-a-secret-deadbeef1234", "PATH=...", "NODE_ENV=production", "PORT=3000"]`.
  The same value delivered by `--mount type=bind,source=<path outside the workspace>,target=/run/moe/env,readonly` => **0 hits**. `.Mounts` printed only `{"Type":"bind","Source":"C:\\...\\env","Destination":"/run/moe/env","RW":false}` — the PATH, never the contents.

WHY THAT IS LOAD-BEARING: platform-secret-canary.e2e.test.ts:218 sweeps `docker inspect <candidate>` stdout for the planted value, and :232 asserts hits === []. So DoD 1 (deliver the environment) and DoD 2 (the canary still finds nothing) are jointly satisfiable by EXACTLY ONE family of designs — a MOUNTED FILE. Any `--env`/`--env-file` delivery turns this row's own DoD 2 red, and DoD 3's phrasing ("not by inspecting the argv the engine assembled") suggests the author may have had argv delivery in mind, so this constraint needs to be stated in the record rather than discovered by the worker at step 5.

THE DESCRIPTION ALREADY POINTS AT IT from the other side: "not a second reading of the variables and not a file written next to the build context". A file, yes — outside the build context, so it can never be committed or swept as a fixture.

WHY THE COMMAND-OVERRIDE SHAPE IS RECOMMENDED: the generated Dockerfile ends `CMD ["node", "${DEPLOYMENT_ENTRY_PATH}"]` (deployment-infrastructure-templates.ts:92) in exec form with NO entrypoint script. Overriding the command to a shell that sources the mounted file and then `exec`s the same entry keeps `process.env` semantics identical between candidate and incumbent — the property that matters, since the same generated app code runs under both — and needs no change to the image, the generator, or the generator's assertions. `docker inspect` then shows a command path and a mount path, no values.

WHY THE DEFECT HID: the generated `/health` route is a pure function touching no database, so a candidate with no DATABASE_URL still reports healthy and passes the deploy's own gate. That is also why DoD 3 insists on a route that ECHOES a marker rather than reusing `/health`.

RAIL 20 CONSUMER CENSUS, done: `runCandidateArgv`'s shape is pinned by deploy-service.test.ts:160 and deploy-rollback.test.ts:111, :125 and :142 — the last indexes the argv POSITIONALLY, so it fails in the least obvious way. All four are in this plan's files.
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE DoD-1/DoD-2 COLLISION IS THE ROW'S CENTRAL HAZARD. A worker who reaches for `--env` will satisfy DoD 1, pass the daemon lane, and only discover the conflict when the docker-gated canary runs at step 5 — after the design is written. Step 1(b) front-loads the measurement for exactly this reason, and step 6's first drill reproduces it through the production path so the constraint is a fact in the record.

2. PLAINTEXT ON DISK FOR THE CONTAINER'S LIFETIME is a new exposure this fix creates. Owner-only mode, outside the workspace, collision-free name, removed when the candidate is gone — and something has to remove it when the deploy refuses partway or the daemon dies mid-deploy. The canary sanctions exactly one plaintext location today (the workspace `.env`, gitignored, asserted at :247); a second one must justify itself in the code.

3. PARTIAL DELIVERY IS WORSE THAN NONE, and the delivery seam says so itself (environment-delivery.ts:124-126: one unopenable seal refuses the WHOLE delivery). The deploy must inherit that and forward `ENV_NAME_INVALID` / `ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE` unchanged, the way deploy-migration-context.ts:119 already does. Drill (ii) exists to prove it.

4. THE COMMAND OVERRIDE COULD DISTURB THE HEALTH GATE. `healthArgv` reads `.State.Health.Status`, which comes from the image's HEALTHCHECK rather than from CMD, so it should survive — but that is a prediction and the worker must measure it, because a candidate that never reports healthy fails the deploy's own gate.

5. ROLLBACK MAY NEED THE SAME TREATMENT. rollback-restore.ts:17 already reads through `readEnvironmentDelivery`; check whether a restored container is started by the same path and gets the same mount, or whether this fix leaves rollback delivering nothing.

6. THE E2E LEGS BIND REAL HOST PORTS (3000 and 5432) and cannot run in parallel with each other — the canary's own header at :42-47. Use `--no-file-parallelism` and run one file at a time.

7. `pnpm test` does not cover apps/** at all; `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` is the owned-package leg DoD 4 names.
